ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-51 and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Article L.561-2-2 CMF (UBO and PEP definitions); Loi Sapin II no. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016; Ordonnance no. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 transposing EU Directive 2018/843; Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) maintained by INPI pursuant to Article R.561-2-2 CMF and Article L.123-9 of the Commercial Code; Decree no. 2021-1158 of 8 September 2021 (Tracfin procedures and national asset-freezing file under Articles L.562-1 et seq. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin where that state is a Party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise French Consular Legalization at the French Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the foreign corporate founder's articles of association (statuts) in currently effective wording
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or public notary of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, as applicable, French Consular Legalization; sworn French translation (traduction assermentee) required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (pouvoir) authorizing the French incorporator or counsel to execute and file the SAS incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative of the foreign corporate founder, certified before a notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport or national identity card of each identifiable ultimate beneficial owner of the franchise group
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent public authority of the natural person's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization; sworn French translation if required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, shareholders, directors, presidents, and ultimate beneficial owners against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) the French national asset-freezing file under Articles L.562-1 et seq. CMF; (iv) the OFAC SDN List as a group-wide best practice for USD-denominated franchise royalty wires; and (v) Tracfin typologies. Politically Exposed Persons and their family members and close associates are identified under Article L.561-2-2 CMF and are subject to enhanced due diligence with senior-management approval. Screening evidence, including negative-news and beneficial-owner verification, is recorded for at least five years in accordance with AMLD5 retention rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI (https://data.inpi.fr) and the Guichet Unique des Formalites des Entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), interfaced with the commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS name may be freely chosen in any language provided it is rendered in Latin-alphabet characters for the RNE index. A brand name expressed in non-Latin script, such as the Chinese characters of the global franchise mother brand, must be accompanied by its official Latin transliteration in the articles of association and in the registration filing. The corporate name must include the legal form designation Societe par Actions Simplifiee or the abbreviation SAS in all commercial documents. The name must not be contrary to public policy (Article 1833 of the Civil Code), must not create confusion with a previously registered legal person, and must not infringe prior trademark rights (Articles L.711-1 et seq. of the Intellectual Property Code), including INPI and EUIPO marks covering the Boba Tea brand in restaurant services (class 43) and tea and syrups (classes 30 and 32).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by the RNE/INPI registrar or the greffe, the applicant may within ten working days either (i) file a revised name through the Guichet Unique, or (ii) submit written observations to the INPI helpdesk for reconsideration. Where rejection is grounded on identity with an earlier legal person or on a prior protected trademark, the incorporator may initiate an action before the tribunal judiciaire within the applicable limitation period to expunge the conflicting registration or to obtain a trademark coexistence or assignment agreement. Where rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, a prior written authorization from the competent ministry or professional order must be obtained and re-filed. As the registration act is jurisdictional in nature, a manifestly unlawful refusal may also be challenged before the judge supervising the registry (juge commis a la surveillance du registre) of the competent tribunal de commerce. This SOP is governed by Articles L.123-9, R.123-7 and R.123-30 of the Commercial Code and Decree no. 2020-1066 of 7 August 2020.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible on a transitional basis under Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-166 of the Commercial Code, provided the domiciliation provider is a licensed approved commercial agent (domiciliataire agree) and the domiciliation is limited to five years. For the franchise licensing and syrups supply chain business, a purely virtual registered office is acceptable at incorporation and during the pilot phase, but sustainable commercial and tax substance requires a physical operational site within two years, comprising at minimum a licensed foodservice kitchen or pilot store and a storage facility for imported tea and syrups, to satisfy DGCCRF inspection competence, EU customs and import status, and DGFiP substance analysis.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated. With only a virtual registered office and no physical foodservice or storage site, the likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection within 24 months is estimated at 70-80% once the food business operator registration is entered in the DGCCRF database; with a leased pilot store and supply warehouse, the estimated risk falls to 35-45%. DGFiP tax audit statistics additionally indicate a heightened probability of desk-based substance challenges for SAS entities domiciled solely at a virtual office address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), including Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-9 (commercial companies), L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 (SAS), and R. 123-1 et seq. (company registration formalities). The SAS articles of association determine its governance, subject to mandatory statutory rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Commercial and Companies Registry (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS), maintained by the relevant commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce); applications are submitted through the national Guichet unique managed by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation declaration (formality of creation) filed through the Guichet unique, accompanied by the signed articles of association (statuts) and supporting documents; registration results in an RCS registration and a SIREN number.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies; the articles must state the share capital, which may be €1. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations; the deposit certificate is included in the filing, and funds are released after registration. In-kind contributions are generally fully contributed at formation and may require a contribution auditor, subject to statutory exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President of [Company Name] SAS, having reviewed the signed articles of association and the capital-deposit certificate, resolves that the Company accepts subscriptions for [number] shares with a total nominal value of €[amount], of which €[amount] has been paid in cash. The registered office is established at [full address] as provided in the articles. [Name] is appointed President for the term and with the powers specified in the articles. [Name] is appointed [Director General, if applicable] on the terms set out in the articles. The President is authorized to complete registration formalities, make required declarations, and open the Company’s operating bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Set SAS governance and execute articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders; professional advice may be obtained from a French lawyer or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the company name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, contributions, President, and any optional officers. Draft articles consistent with the Commercial Code and intended governance. Have all subscribers sign the articles; notarization is generally not required for ordinary cash contributions. Use a notarial deed where an immovable-property contribution or another legally required notarial act is involved.
required_dossiers: Final articles of association signed by all subscribers
Identity and address details of subscribers and proposed officers
Evidence of authority for any corporate subscriber
Registered-office occupancy evidence or domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies between the articles, capital-deposit evidence, officer details, and online declaration. Obtain required signatures or corporate authorizations and resubmit the corrected documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit cash capital and publish formation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations; habilitated legal-announcement journal (journal d’annonces légales) in the registered-office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit at least 50% of cash contributions into a formation account and obtain the deposit certificate. Arrange publication of the prescribed formation notice in a habilitated journal for the department of the registered office and retain the publication certificate. Publication is mandatory; the notice fee varies by department and statutory notice length.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association or draft articles accepted by the depositary
Subscriber and beneficial-owner identification required by the depositary
Capital-deposit certificate
Legal-announcement publication certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve depositary identity or source-of-funds queries with requested evidence. Correct and republish a notice containing material errors, then include the corrected publication certificate in the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for company registration and disclose beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, electronically routed to the competent local RCS registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company-creation formality electronically, select the appropriate commercial activity, upload the signed articles and supporting evidence, and declare beneficial owners through the required beneficial-ownership filing. Pay the applicable registry charges shown in the portal. Provide translations or certified copies where requested for foreign-language or foreign-issued documents; apostille or legalization requirements depend on document origin and applicable conventions.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association
Capital-deposit certificate
Registered-office evidence
Formation-notice publication certificate
President’s identity document and non-conviction/parentage declaration, as applicable
Identity and ownership information for beneficial owners
Authority documents for corporate subscribers or representatives
Any regulated-activity declaration or permit applicable to the actual operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the Guichet unique dashboard and respond within the stated deadline to registry requests. Correct rejected fields or documents, pay any additional charge, and resubmit. Escalate a persistent registry dispute to the competent registry or use the available formal appeal procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, competent tax office (service des impôts des entreprises), and selected bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the RCS registration evidence, SIREN and SIRET identifiers, and Kbis extract. Complete bank account activation and release of deposited capital. Confirm corporate-tax and VAT registration treatment, invoicing settings, accounting records, and any applicable payroll registrations before hiring. Keep the beneficial-owner information and corporate records current.
required_dossiers: RCS registration evidence and Kbis extract
Articles and capital-deposit evidence
Bank account documentation
Tax and VAT registration information
Employment and payroll details, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax, VAT, or identity data with the competent authority. If bank funds remain blocked, provide the registration evidence and satisfy the depositary’s release requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial licensing board or manufacturing permit applies to an ordinary bubble-tea franchise outlet. The competent municipal authority (mairie) handles applicable public-access building and works formalities; the departmental Directorate for the Protection of Populations (DDPP) oversees relevant food-safety requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating license is required for an ordinary non-alcoholic bubble-tea outlet. A food-business establishment handling products of animal origin must make the applicable prior declaration to the DDPP before opening. Food-hygiene training requirements apply to qualifying commercial catering activity; at least one person must hold the required training or a statutory exemption must apply. Alcohol sales, if added, require the applicable municipal alcohol license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique); the relevant Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (DREAL) or departmental authority administers applicable environmental procedures.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-specific EIA and ICPE authorization for a standard retail beverage outlet. Screening or authorization may be required if the site or equipment falls within a listed project or ICPE threshold; assess the specific premises, processes, and capacity before works or operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the local public sewer connection and wastewater-discharge rules, including any applicable pretreatment requirements. No general VOC threshold is specific to a typical tea outlet; applicable emissions and waste obligations depend on installed equipment and any ICPE classification. Segregate and dispose of food, packaging, oils, and other waste through authorized channels and comply with local waste-sorting rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises will generally be an établissement recevant du public (ERP). Before opening, comply with applicable fire-safety and accessibility rules, obtain any required mairie authorization for construction or material alterations, and complete required inspections or commission procedures where applicable. Maintain fire-safety equipment, evacuation arrangements, and ERP records. Comply with occupational health and safety obligations, including workplace risk assessment and a documented DUERP; no universal structural-load clearance is required absent relevant works, equipment, or building-specific requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), official portal: https://www.impots.gouv.fr/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS obtain SIREN/SIRET from INSEE; foreign entities register via guichet unique for statutory TIN/VAT ID
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No standard check-the-box elections available; French SAS subject to entity-level corporate taxation under the IS regime

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) for B2B transactions with real-time reporting and digital stamping via authorized platforms

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods exported outside the EU upon proof of export; offshore services qualify under specific conditions
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims result in penalties up to 80% of evaded tax, interest charges, and potential criminal liability with retrospective VAT adjustments

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange policy is governed principally by European Union law and administered domestically, where relevant, by the French Treasury Directorate General (Direction générale du Trésor) of the Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general exchange controls. Current-account payments, including imports, franchise royalties, service fees, dividends, interest, and ordinary commercial remittances, are generally freely transferable, subject to sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, tax withholding and transfer-pricing requirements. Capital-account transactions are also generally liberalized under EU free-movement principles, but foreign direct investment in protected strategic sectors may require prior authorization or notification. A French SAS may hold foreign-currency accounts and may retain foreign-currency receipts. Profit distributions require distributable profits, approved accounts and shareholder approval; dividends may be subject to French withholding tax, treaty relief or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions. Interest, royalties and management fees require arm's-length support, beneficial-owner verification and applicable withholding-tax analysis. Banks may delay or refuse transfers lacking a clear economic purpose, supporting contracts, tax evidence, source-of-funds evidence or sanctions clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a French bank, convert export receipts into euros or convert a prescribed percentage of foreign-currency receipts. No general statutory repatriation deadline applies solely because proceeds arise from exports or international franchise activity. Export proceeds may be received into euro or foreign-currency accounts, subject to contractual settlement terms, accounting recognition, VAT and customs documentation, bank transaction-monitoring requirements and applicable statistical reporting. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more into or out of the European Union require customs declaration by the traveler or carrier. Banks and designated reporting entities may request transaction information for Banque de France balance-of-payments and statistical reporting. Sector-specific sanctions, export-control, customs and tax rules may impose additional restrictions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant regional Crédit Agricole caisse
Groupe BPCE, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for a supplementary operational account and Low to Medium as the sole treasury bank. An EU-authorized electronic money institution or payment institution may provide EUR payment accounts, SEPA transfers, cards and certain foreign-exchange services under passporting or applicable local authorization. It does not replace a French bank for every capital-deposit, escrow, lending, cash-management, cheque, guarantee or documentary-trade requirement. The institution must identify the SAS, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, controllers, source of funds, expected payment corridors, franchise counterparties and high-risk geographies. Client-money safeguarding is not equivalent to French deposit-guarantee protection. Offshore digital EMIs without applicable EU authorization, passporting or a regulated EU partner should not be used for core receipts or capital funding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding is legally and commercially possible where the institution can complete reliable identity verification, beneficial-owner identification, electronic-signature validation, source-of-funds review and risk-based enhanced due diligence. In practice, banks may require an in-person meeting, notarized or legalized documents, original documents, video interviews or a local representative for a newly incorporated SAS, non-resident shareholders, complex ownership, unusual payment corridors or higher-risk jurisdictions. The legal representative normally signs the account mandate; all persons with authority to operate the account and relevant ultimate beneficial owners must be identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered ownership involving offshore companies, nominee shareholders, trusts or an inability to identify the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current French corporate extract or registration evidence; articles of association; complete ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; shareholder registers; certificates of incorporation and good standing for foreign entities; passports and proof of address; director and authorized-signatory resolutions; beneficial-owner declaration; explanation of control rights and a signed ownership certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital funding or operating funds received from a third party, newly formed holding company or jurisdiction viewed by the bank as elevated risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; bank statements showing source accumulation; audited financial statements or tax returns of the funding party; sale, dividend or financing evidence where relevant; proof of beneficial ownership of the funding party; payment instruction identifying the exact economic purpose; sanctions and adverse-media screening record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unexplained inbound franchise royalties, syrup purchases, intercompany charges or payments inconsistent with the stated bubble-tea franchise business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Franchise, supply, trademark and distribution agreements; invoices; purchase orders; delivery and customs records; pricing policy; transfer-pricing support; expected-volume schedule; counterparties' registration and ownership data; explanation of payment corridors; VAT treatment; reconciliation between contracts, invoices, customs records and bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned persons, sanctioned territories, restricted goods, dual-use products or a counterparty with adverse sanctions or corruption indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due-diligence file; sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-user statement; product classification; customs and export-control analysis; beneficial-owner confirmation; contractual sanctions clause; shipping documents; documented escalation and legal sign-off where a potential match is identified. Do not process a transaction while a genuine sanctions concern remains unresolved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders unable to provide acceptable proof of address, tax residence or identity documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent utility bill, bank statement or government-issued residence document; certified translation where required; valid passport or national identity document; tax-residence certificate; notarization, apostille or legalization when requested; video-identification record; local attorney or accountant confirmation; documented explanation of residential and tax status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive point-of-sale activity, unexplained cash deposits or weak controls over franchisee collections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS-provider agreements; cash-handling policy; daily till reconciliation; store-level sales reports; deposit records; segregation-of-duties matrix; franchisee settlement schedule; refund and chargeback controls; internal audit reports; suspicious-activity escalation procedure; evidence that cash deposits correspond to recorded sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax or regulatory inconsistency, including missing beneficial-owner filing, overdue accounts, unexplained tax arrears or unsupported royalty deductions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date French corporate filings; beneficial-owner filing evidence; tax registration and VAT details; filed tax returns; payment certificates or approved payment plans; annual accounts; statutory registers; tax-residence certificates; withholding-tax analysis; transfer-pricing documentation; explanation of any filing delay.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in share capital to the SAS capital-deposit account opened in the company's name or through the formation professional handling the deposit. Use EUR SEPA Credit Transfer where available, otherwise SWIFT cross-border transfer with complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, ultimate-beneficiary and purpose information. The payment reference should state the subscriber, SAS legal name, capital subscription or shareholder-loan purpose, and relevant agreement or resolution. The bank will normally require the draft or executed articles, subscription form, shareholder or board resolution, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence and identification of the remitter. The depositary issues a certificate of deposit after cleared funds are received; funds are released to the operational account after registration evidence is provided. A shareholder loan must be routed and documented as debt rather than capital, with a written agreement, arm's-length terms, accounting treatment and any applicable French tax, interest-withholding and transfer-pricing analysis. Do not route capital through unrelated personal accounts or unidentified third parties. For non-EU investors or protected sectors, conduct French foreign-investment authorization and reporting analysis before funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant where supported for EUR suppliers within the SEPA area. Use SWIFT cross-border payment messaging, commonly an MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 customer-credit-transfer message, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency settlements. A commercial letter of credit may be issued or confirmed by a bank under UCP 600; documentary collections may use URC 522. Match each payment to a purchase order, invoice, contract, customs entry, transport document and goods or services description. For syrup and equipment imports, retain customs classification, import declarations, origin documents, transport records and VAT evidence. For franchise royalties, retain the franchise agreement, royalty calculation, invoice, withholding-tax review, transfer-pricing support and evidence of beneficial ownership. Use SHA, OUR or BEN fee allocation consistently with the contract. Apply sanctions, export-control, anti-bribery and dual-use screening before release. Maintain segregation between operating payments, payroll, tax payments, franchisee settlements and intercompany transfers. French banks may request transaction-purpose information, but France does not generally use a universal statutory purpose-code system equivalent to certain exchange-controlled jurisdictions; use the bank's internal payment purpose taxonomy accurately.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm, supported by documented forecast or committed exposures and appropriate treasury limits.

Non-deliverable forwards where the reference currency, counterparty, settlement method and legal documentation are permitted by the relevant regulated institution; NDFs are cash-settled and may not be suitable where the company requires physical currency delivery.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented recurring or longer-term currency and funding exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms and EMIR requirements.

Foreign-exchange options, collars and other derivatives may be used subject to MiFID II classification, appropriateness or suitability requirements where applicable, disclosure, valuation and accounting controls.

Hedging must be linked to genuine commercial or financing exposures, not speculative activity; maintain hedge-designation records, counterparty confirmations, mark-to-market controls, collateral monitoring, liquidity stress testing and IFRS or French GAAP hedge-accounting documentation.

Use regulated EU or equivalent authorized counterparties and confirm reporting, clearing, margin, collateral and trade-repository obligations under EMIR and applicable French financial-services rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; approval by the shareholders or sole shareholder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president may be subject to a fine of up to EUR 9,000; a court may order approval and impose a daily penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing and management report, where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe) at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure may result in a fine of up to EUR 1,500, doubled for repeat offences, and a court injunction subject to a daily penalty; persistent non-compliance may prompt registry or judicial measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year company, generally the second working day after 1 May, subject to the administration's electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased in specified circumstances, plus late-payment interest; omissions or inaccuracies may trigger additional penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate property contribution (CFE) declaration or payment, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally payable by 15 December; an establishment declaration is generally due by 31 December of the year of creation, and subsequent annual declarations are required only in specified circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally incurs a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest; failure to submit a required declaration may result in tax reassessment and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, if information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after a change to reportable beneficial ownership information; no routine annual confirmation is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate required information may lead to a court injunction, criminal fines, and, for responsible individuals, possible imprisonment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of these thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 employees. Specific group, control, and regulated-entity rules may require an auditor independently of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Commercial Code and the applicable ANC regulations for individual statutory accounts. IFRS is required for consolidated accounts of companies within the relevant EU-listed-company regime; other groups may use IFRS where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no general annual UBO confirmation filing. The company must keep beneficial ownership information current and file changes within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the company's share-movement records and reflected in the register of beneficial owners when they alter reportable information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share movements and shareholders' individual securities accounts, maintained at the registered office
Shareholder decision records and minutes, maintained at the registered office
Register of beneficial owners and supporting information, maintained or made available as required by law

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200-800 per year, depending on location and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-15,000 per year for a small SAS; higher for complex groups or regulated activities

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
